Hi John —

Great to speak earlier. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment before the technical deep-dive: 

- Latency targets: 95th percentile <= 700ms for text-generation (avg prompt+completion ~ 600 tokens).
- Throughput: sustained ~500 requests/minute during peak bursts, with short spikes up to ~1,000 req/min.
- Concurrency: expected ~1,200 concurrent active sessions (long-lived streaming sessions for chat agents) and ~3,000 parallel short API requests across your fleet.
- Streaming requirements: SSE/websocket-style streaming for long-lived agents with mid-session partial responses; we need stable per-connection keep-alive and reconnection semantics.
- Connection pooling: you prefer client-side pooling with HTTP/2 multiplexing where possible; looking for guidance on connection counts and timeouts.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll send a first-pass quota/proposal that maps your concurrency + burst needs to Redwood hosted limits vs Dedicated pool sizing.
2) Schedule technical deep-dive with Logan (solutions engineer) to review traffic patterns and streaming behavior.
3) If numbers look good, pilot with a small dedicated pool + canary traffic.

I attached a short proposal with baseline numbers — see attachment in my next email. Can you confirm the concurrency numbers above are accurate and who from your infrastructure/procurement teams should be included?

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — that summary looks right. A couple clarifying Qs before the deep-dive: 

1) Our "concurrent active sessions" number (1,200) represents long-lived user sessions where the connection remains open for streaming updates (avg session length ~45 minutes). Is Redwood able to support that many concurrent streaming connections on Hosted, or will we need Dedicated?

2) For the 3,000 parallel short API requests, is rate limiting calculated per-account or per-route? We have a few heavy routes (batch summarize, rerank) that we'd like to isolate so a per-route quota would be ideal.

3) On connection pooling: our infra team typically keeps 50 active connections per host and uses HTTP/2 multiplexing. Any Redwood-specific recommended best practices?

I’ve looped in procurement and Priya (infra). We can set aside an hour Tue/Wed for the deep-dive.

Subject: Re: ACME - Concurrency & Rate Limits follow-up

John — thanks, useful questions. First-pass answers and a proposed quota attached: 

- Streaming concurrency: Hosted API has default soft limits on concurrent streaming connections per account (typically ~200-300) to ensure fair usage; for sustained 1,200 concurrent streaming sessions we recommend Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) or a hosted Enterprise quota uplift. Dedicated provides predictable capacity and removes multi-tenant soft limits.

- Per-route quotas: Yes. We support per-route rate limits and can set separate quotas for heavy routes (e.g., rerank/summarize) vs chat. We'll include per-route ceilings in the proposal.

- Connection pooling: Your 50-connections approach with HTTP/2 is sensible. For long-lived streaming we recommend: keep-alive enabled, idle timeout ~5min client-side, reuse connections for multiple sessions when possible. If you use HTTP/2, multiplexing reduces required connections but watch for head-of-line issues on large payloads — we can advise on max concurrent streams per connection in the deep-dive.

- Proposal summary (see attached PDF):
  * Option A (Hosted quota uplift): support 1,200 streaming connections + 3,000 parallel short requests via quota increase and prioritized routing — suitable if you want to start fast.
  * Option B (Dedicated pool): 4 GPU nodes reserved, autoscale headroom + canary routing, per-route quotas enforced — recommended for SLA and steady load.
  * Pilot plan: 2-week canary at 10% traffic, health checks on latency SLOs, then scale to 50% if stable.

Attachments: 20260817-acme-quota-proposal.pdf (baseline numbers and T&Cs).

Next: can Logan and I take the deep-dive on Tue 10:0011:00 or Wed 14:0015:00 PT? Also please share a sample 24h traffic pattern file so we can size burst capacity.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: 20260817-acme-quota-proposal.pdf]

Hi all — happy to run the technical deep-dive. Tue 10:00 PT works for me. A couple quick notes to prepare: 

- Please share a 24h export of request timestamps + route names (CSV or spreadsheet) and an example of a streaming session (time between partials, avg partial size). That lets us model KV cache reuse and batching efficiency.
- On connection pooling: with HTTP/2 we typically recommend starting with 16–32 connections per host and enabling multiplexing; if you rely heavily on long-lived streaming sessions you may need additional connections to avoid stream starvation. We'll review tradeoffs in the session and show estimated latency impact.
- Rate-limiting model: Redwood can enforce both request-based (requests/sec) and token-based (tokens/sec) quotas. For your rerank route we usually suggest strict request/sec ceilings plus a soft token budget to prevent costly tail events.

Logan
